title: Decision tree for three-sign majority
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $R_1,R_2,B_3\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ satisfy $R_1\cap(R_2\cup B_3)=\varnothing$ and $R_2\cap B_3=\varnothing$, and let a sign mean an element of $\mathbb Z^\times$. Suppose $C_1$ and $C_2$ assign, to each sign, a decision tree querying only coordinates in $R_1$ and $R_2$, respectively, and let $E_3$ be a decision tree querying only coordinates in $B_3$. For any fixed sign $x_1$, the construction gives a decision tree querying only coordinates in $R_1\cup(R_2\cup B_3)$: after the first tree returns $y_1$, it runs the second tree (with input $x_1$) before $E_3$ if $y_1=x_1$, and otherwise runs $E_3$ before the second tree; when the next observed sign equals $y_1$, it returns $y_1$ immediately, and otherwise labels the output by the three-sign majority value of the observed signs.
hypotheses_covered: $C_1$ assigns a decision tree querying only $R_1$ to every sign
$C_2$ assigns a decision tree querying only $R_2$ to every sign
$E_3$ is a decision tree querying only $B_3$
